children.procedure: Run the mapped component tests through `make scientific-acceptance` with an isolated profile.
children.oracle: The assertions in the mapped tests.
children.criteria: Every mapped test executes and passes, with zero skips.

children.requirement: Two kernels and a manual edit share one base; each accepted result records its producer.
children.procedure: In an isolated profile, start two actual confined napari kernels and one manual Labels editor on the same saved input. Each changes it differently and saves; two saves conflict and keep copies. Resolve every result.
children.oracle: Each result names only its own producer (its own cells, or the manual paint action with tool, label, points and view context), the shared base revision and its changed region.
children.criteria: All three producers are actual, including a manual paint edit on an editable Labels layer. tests/test_scientific_provenance_actual.py covers the two kernels only, because the one prepared integration binds an editable Image.

children.requirement: After save and restart, every accepted result resolves its exact producing history, settings and base.
children.procedure: In an isolated profile on the production browser path, save results from one base through the ordinary UI with actual workers (two kernels and a manual edit). Open each from Data, read Controls > Save > Document, inputs and history > How this was made, and follow Open original and Open producing history. Quit and restart the app, reload, and repeat.
children.oracle: Each panel names only its own producer (its own code cells or manual action), its base revision and its changed region, with no problems listed; the provenance endpoint answers byte-identically before and after the restart, and the history each button opens is the recorded one.
children.criteria: Every accepted result resolves, before and after the restart, with saves made through the ordinary UI by actual workers. Synthetic seeded saves do not meet this criterion.

children.requirement: After export, every accepted result resolves its exact producing history, settings and base.
children.procedure: With actual confined kernels as in two-kernels-shared-base, export each accepted result (GET /api/scientific-projects/{id}/bundle or scientific_exchange.export), reimport it into a second profile, and resolve it there.
children.oracle: The resolver answer in the second profile equals the one in the first, with no problems, for every result including conflict copies.
children.criteria: Every result produced by actual workers resolves identically after export and reimport, and the runner executes the check itself. The opt-in test passes with NAPARI_EDITABLE_HOST_PREPARATION, but the runner passes no environment, so no check is registered yet.

children.requirement: Conflict copies resolve their own producing history after save, restart and export.
children.procedure: As save-restart-resolves, with two of the three results refused as conflicts and kept as copies through the ordinary UI. Open each copy from Data, read How this was made, and follow its buttons; restart and repeat; export and reimport when H02 slice 5 exists.
children.oracle: Each copy says it was saved as a separate copy, names its own producer and the base it was copied from, and leaves the original unchanged; the answers are identical after the restart.
children.criteria: Every conflict copy resolves its own producing history after save and restart (and after export once slice 5 exists), with saves made through the ordinary UI by actual workers.

children.requirement: Two kernels and a manual editor share one base and save three different results (one in place, two as conflict copies). After a restart, each result resolves only its own digest-verified base, input, output and producing history: its own code cells or its own manual action with tool, label, points and view context. A copy made of unchanged values keeps their producer, remapped to the copy.
children.procedure: Run the mapped resolver tests through `make scientific-acceptance` on real retained storage and HTTP, with synthetic workers.
children.oracle: The resolved base, history references, cells and actions asserted in the mapped test.
children.criteria: Every mapped test executes and passes, with zero skips.

children.requirement: Every accepted array change carries an exact, bounded change record from retained bytes, whether or not any event announced it: which chunks differ between the recorded input and output, their count and their array bounds.
children.procedure: Run the mapped resolver tests through `make scientific-acceptance` on real retained storage and HTTP, with synthetic workers.
children.oracle: Changed chunk keys, counts and bounds asserted in the mapped test.
children.criteria: Every mapped test executes and passes, with zero skips.

children.requirement: A producing history that cannot be read, belongs to another kernel or another input, or values changed after acceptance are reported as problems. No other history sharing the input is substituted, and kept provenance says the revision that accepted it. An older copy whose record was never remapped says exactly that, and a damaged earlier revision is a reported problem that leaves the rest of the lookup intact.
children.procedure: Run the mapped resolver tests through `make scientific-acceptance` on real retained storage and HTTP, with synthetic workers.
children.oracle: The reported problems and accepted revisions asserted in the mapped tests.
children.criteria: Every mapped test executes and passes, with zero skips.

children.requirement: Values accepted without a recorded producer say so, and a later publication without a record drops the earlier values’ provenance instead of carrying it to new values.
children.procedure: Run the mapped resolver tests through `make scientific-acceptance` on real retained storage and HTTP, with synthetic workers.
children.oracle: The unrecorded producer wording asserted in the mapped test.
children.criteria: Every mapped test executes and passes, with zero skips.

children.requirement: A document save through the Studio API cannot add, change or remove accepted provenance; only owned publication writes it. The provenance endpoint reads it and refuses an invalid session.
children.procedure: Run the mapped resolver tests through `make scientific-acceptance` on real retained storage and HTTP, with synthetic workers.
children.oracle: The refusals, unchanged revision and endpoint answers asserted in the mapped tests.
children.criteria: Every mapped test executes and passes, with zero skips.

children.requirement: The accepted record keeps, atomically with the revision, the integration and runtime versions, the coordinate space, the chunk change record and a plain statement of what was not recorded (randomness, environment, files, network, unattributed callback changes); a saved change record that disagrees with the bytes is reported.
children.procedure: Run the mapped resolver tests through `make scientific-acceptance` on real retained storage and HTTP, with synthetic workers.
children.oracle: The retained record fields and the reported disagreement asserted in the mapped tests.
children.criteria: Every mapped test executes and passes, with zero skips.

children.procedure: Run the mapped path tests through `make scientific-acceptance` on real retained storage, with synthetic workers.
children.criteria: Every mapped test executes and passes, with zero skips.
children.requirement: One acceptance boundary explains every publication path the same way: a multi-layer save after a lost acknowledgement (one revision, every layer resolved to its producer), two multi-layer saves from one base (an explicit conflict whose copy keeps its own producer), a new output after a failed publication is retried, and a producer record Hooke cannot check, which is kept as given and never shown as verified.
children.oracle: Resolved layers, producers, revisions, copies and the unverified marking asserted in the mapped tests.

children.procedure: Run the mapped path tests through `make scientific-acceptance` on real retained storage, with synthetic workers.
children.criteria: Every mapped test executes and passes, with zero skips.
children.requirement: An edit undone before saving keeps its paint and undo actions and records no changed values; an edit undone and redone keeps all three actions and its one changed block; a value written in place with no event or action appears in the change record, and the record says such changes are not attributed to an action.
children.oracle: Changed chunk keys, bounds, recorded actions and the not-attributed statement asserted in the mapped tests.

children.procedure: Run the mapped exchange tests through `make scientific-acceptance` on real retained storage, zip bundles and HTTP, with synthetic workers.
children.criteria: Every mapped test executes and passes, with zero skips.
children.requirement: Exporting an accepted result carries its revision records, its original, its producing history and their saved values as exact bytes under portable names (lower-case hex, forward slashes); reimported into another profile, through the store or HTTP, each of the two kernels’ and the manual editor’s results resolves exactly as it did, also after a restart, and only its own producer travels with it.
children.oracle: Equal resolver answers, carried documents, portable names and HTTP responses asserted in the mapped tests.

children.procedure: Run the mapped exchange tests through `make scientific-acceptance` on real retained storage, zip bundles and HTTP, with synthetic workers.
children.criteria: Every mapped test executes and passes, with zero skips.
children.requirement: Reimport validates every revision with the store’s own checks and every array and file reference on a complete staged copy before anything is visible: a bundle missing a chunk or manifest, with an unreadable revision, an invalid or unreferenced extra document, a damaged, mis-targeted or path-escaping entry, or work beyond the allowance imports nothing and leaves no files. It is idempotent, extends a shorter history, repairs a damaged copy the profile holds, never overwrites a different document with the same identity, holds each document’s lock so a racing save cannot overwrite an imported revision, and takes back what it placed if a later step fails.
children.oracle: The unchanged profile, the refusals and the extended history asserted in the mapped tests.

children.requirement: New-output validation and atomic publication with controlled workers.
children.procedure: Run the mapped component tests through `make scientific-acceptance` with an isolated profile.
children.oracle: The assertions in the mapped tests.
children.criteria: Every mapped test executes and passes, with zero skips.

children.requirement: A Python kernel creates a new Image output; it is accepted and reopens with exact data and relations.
children.procedure: With a prepared private review bundle (`NAPARI_NATIVE_HOST_PREPARATION`), open a retained source revision in the actual confined napari worker through scientific_project_review.review. Python in Hooke's console makes all seven layer types after startup, and napari's builtin npe2 plugin makes Image, Labels and Points (its balls_2d sample), Shapes (its writer, then its CSV reader) and Surface (its OBJ reader). OutputSave accepts each as a new output, and a fresh review of that output reopens it. Run by tests/test_scientific_outputs_upstream.py in `make scientific-acceptance`.
children.oracle: The reopened layer has exactly the type, data arrays (dtype, shape and bytes), data-to-world mapping and shape types it was saved with. The output names the exact source revision and digest as its base and its producer, and the source revision is unchanged.
children.criteria: The mapped parametrized cases execute on the actual worker and pass with zero skips.

P1.axis-position.step-1-open-the-5d-reso.criteria: Five sliders; t, c, z shown with ranges 0-4, 0-2, 0-6 and y, x displayed; nsteps equal the shape; the opening steps equal napari's; the centre probe equals the voxel's own index. P1.axis-position.qtdims-nsliders.procedure: Isolated profile: a new Chromium profile (HOOKE_BROWSER) on a private orchestrator with an empty home, no camera and the Studio rebuilt from the checkout (its build identity must equal the backend). The asymmetric TCZYX uint16 fixture (5x3x7x11x13, each voxel holding its flat index) is a saved scene document of the prepared review integration (NAPARI_NATIVE_HOST_PREPARATION). It is opened from Project Data (Open result, then Open session) and calibrated in the session's Python panel: scale 2.5/1/0.75/0.4/0.3, translate 10/0/-3/5/7, axis labels t/c/z/y/x, units second/pixel/micrometer.  Then: Open the 5D document from Project Data before calibration; read the Dimensions sliders, their ranges and which axes are displayed, and probe the centre voxel.
P1.axis-position.qtdims-nsliders.oracle: Three ways: what the Studio shows and the actual review worker's native state (one shared napari snapshot, read through the Python panel) must equal the same steps in a plain pinned napari Viewer process on the prepared runtime's own Python (tests/scientific_napari_reference.py), and the values the fixture's definition gives independently (tests/scientific_dims_fixture.py). Executed by tests/test_scientific_dims_browser.py::test_open_5d_resource_from_project_data_shows_every_axis, and by the harness self-check test_the_comparison_catches_a_worker_whose_napari_behaviour_was_broken, which breaks napari inside the worker and needs the same comparisons to fail.
P1.axis-position.qtdims-nsliders.criteria: One slider per dimension (5), equal to napari's ndim; displayed axes hidden.
P1.axis-position.qtdims-nsliders.hooke_equivalent: Project Data > Open result > Open session; View > Dimensions sliders

P1.axis-position.shortcut-napari-focus-a.procedure: Isolated profile: a new Chromium profile (HOOKE_BROWSER) on a private orchestrator with an empty home, no camera and the Studio rebuilt from the checkout (its build identity must equal the backend). The asymmetric TCZYX uint16 fixture (5x3x7x11x13, each voxel holding its flat index) is a saved scene document of the prepared review integration (NAPARI_NATIVE_HOST_PREPARATION). It is opened from Project Data (Open result, then Open session) and calibrated in the session's Python panel: scale 2.5/1/0.75/0.4/0.3, translate 10/0/-3/5/7, axis labels t/c/z/y/x, units second/pixel/micrometer.  Then: Click the preview to focus it; press Right, Right, Left, Option/Alt+Up, Right, Option/Alt+Down, Option/Alt+Down, Left; then press Next slice, Keyboard axis up, Previous slice and Keyboard axis down.
P1.axis-position.shortcut-napari-focus-a.oracle: Three ways: what the Studio shows and the actual review worker's native state (one shared napari snapshot, read through the Python panel) must equal the same steps in a plain pinned napari Viewer process on the prepared runtime's own Python (tests/scientific_napari_reference.py), and the values the fixture's definition gives independently (tests/scientific_dims_fixture.py). Executed by tests/test_scientific_dims_browser.py::test_napari_dimension_shortcuts_step_and_focus_the_keyboard_axis, and by the harness self-check test_the_comparison_catches_a_worker_whose_napari_behaviour_was_broken, which breaks napari inside the worker and needs the same comparisons to fail.
P1.axis-position.shortcut-napari-focus-a.criteria: Option/Alt+Down, delivered to the focused preview, runs focus_axes_down.
P1.axis-position.shortcut-napari-focus-a.hooke_equivalent: Preview keyboard (napari default bindings) and View > Dimensions: Previous/Next slice, Keyboard axis up/down

It is opened from Project Data (Open result, then Open session) and calibrated in the session's Python panel: scale 2.5/1/0.75/0.4/0.3, translate 10/0/-3/5/7, axis labels t/c/z/y/x, units second/pixel/micrometer.  Then: In the Python panel set viewer.dims.rollable with t locked and press Roll axes; unlock; then set_range on z, assign viewer.dims.range, assign viewer.dims.nsteps and call viewer.dims.reset(); press Check current view after each and read every axis line.
P1.axis-position.dims-reset.oracle: Three ways: what the Studio shows and the actual review worker's native state (one shared napari snapshot, read through the Python panel) must equal the same steps in a plain pinned napari Viewer process on the prepared runtime's own Python (tests/scientific_napari_reference.py), and the values the fixture's definition gives independently (tests/scientific_dims_fixture.py). Executed by tests/test_scientific_dims_browser.py::test_dims_rollable_range_steps_and_reset_through_python_are_napari_s, and by the harness self-check test_the_comparison_catches_a_worker_whose_napari_behaviour_was_broken, which breaks napari inside the worker and needs the same comparisons to fail.
P1.axis-position.dims-reset.criteria: reset() gives napari's (0, 2, 1) ranges, zero points, natural order and unlocked axes, shown on every axis.
P1.axis-position.dims-reset.hooke_equivalent: The session's Python panel (napari Dims API in the worker), shown in View > Dimensions; Roll axes

P1.playback.loopmode-once.procedure: Isolated profile: a new Chromium profile (HOOKE_BROWSER) on a private orchestrator with an empty home, no camera and the Studio rebuilt from the checkout (its build identity must equal the backend). The asymmetric TCZYX uint16 fixture (5x3x7x11x13, each voxel holding its flat index) is a saved scene document of the prepared review integration (NAPARI_NATIVE_HOST_PREPARATION). Then: Play t from 1..3 at 10 per second: Once forward from 1 and from 3, Once backward from 3; Loop and Back and forth forward from 1 and Loop backward from 3, pressing Stop after 7, 7 and 5 slices. At 2 per second: Loop from 1 (Stop after 3), Once 1..4 from 1 and from 4. Then enter First 3, Last 1 and press Play.
P1.playback.loopmode-once.oracle: Three ways: the slices the Studio requested, each frame the worker returned for it and whether its pixels were fetched to draw, against (a) napari's own QtDims.play/AnimationThread driven in a plain pinned napari Viewer process on the prepared runtime's Python (its frames in order and the time of the first), and (b) sequences written out independently from AnimationThread's rules. Executed by tests/test_scientific_dims_browser.py::test_playback_plays_each_loop_mode_both_directions_stops_and_refuses_invalid_ranges, and by the harness self-check test_the_comparison_catches_a_worker_whose_napari_behaviour_was_broken, which breaks napari inside the worker and needs the same comparisons to fail.
P1.playback.loopmode-once.criteria: Once plays to the last frame and stops; started on the last frame it starts again at the first; backward reaches the first and stops.

P3.points.api-colormanager-categorical-c.procedure: Open the saved 3D fixture from DATA in the production Studio on an isolated profile, start its session, add the Points layer (six points on three slices; categorical kind, float area and uint64 id features) in the Python section, set View › marker style › Face and Border colors (direct, cycle by kind, colormap by area) and Apply, then read the native layer in the Python section. The same changes run as frame-bound requests in Hooke's actual review worker with renders at an explicit camera.
P3.points.api-colormanager-categorical-c.oracle: Plain pinned napari in a confined reference process doing the same through its public API: every observation equal and renders equal to the pixel. Independent: the ColorManager’s categorical_colormap maps each category to the cycle color of its first appearance.
P3.points.api-colormanager-categorical-c.criteria: The browser journey and the actual-worker comparison both execute and pass with zero skips against the prepared runtimes, refused settings change nothing, and the harness self-check fails when napari's Points.symbol setter and Shapes.move_to_front are broken inside the worker; coordinates and feature values stay unchanged at every step.
